text:
cheng: quick heads-up — did an nsys capture on ded-dev during the nightly perf run. Seeing repeated kernel selection flips (fp16_kernel_v2 <-> fp16_kernel_alt) across batches when KV cache warmup is incomplete. capture flags used: --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt, duration ~12s. attaching notes.

maria: can you paste the exact CLI and any NVTX markers you used? curious about sampling config.

cheng: here it is (ran from the node):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=nsys_cheng_3629 -f true --sample=cpu --sampling-frequency=1000 --duration=12 --capture-range=nvtx
```
I wrapped kv cache warmup with nvtx ranges and also instrumented batching entry/exit.

kyle: interesting. two guesses: sample window too short so OSRT sampling biases which kernel looks hottest, or there's an actual heuristic flip when batch size crosses 8 tokens. did you correlate with KV eviction NVTX?

cheng: yes — the kernel flip aligns with an `kv_evict` NVTX range right before the first tokens of the batch. timeline shows a small gap and then the runtime picks the alternate kernel. looks like a fallback path when cache misses are detected.

sam: can you repro with longer capture? 12s might miss steady state. try 30s and bracketed capture so we only profile the steady infer loop. also set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` to keep it isolated.

maria: also try `--sample=gpu` (we usually do that for kernel selection noise) and increase sampling-frequency to 2000. that helped remove sampling aliasing in the past. example: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=nsys_repro -f true --sample=gpu --sampling-frequency=2000 --duration=30 --capture-range=nvtx
```

kyle: if it is KV eviction causing a switch, we should see corresponding OSRT markers around memcpy/evict kernels. check kernel names and launch params in the timeline (seq len, batch id). sometimes the runtime encodes the quantization path in the kernel suffix.

cheng: pulled out a short excerpt from the timeline: kernel A runs ~900us, then `kv_evict` CPU op, then kernel B runs ~1.2ms. nvprof shows different shared-memory config between A and B. suspect kernel selector toggles based on cache hit ratio.

ops-bot: deploybot: FYI — rollout 2026-03-12 changed batching heuristics (PR #4521). Might be relevant.

sam: oh nice catch, ops-bot. @cheng can you run the repro on the commit before PR #4521 (we have an old image tagged `perf-baseline-20260310`)? that would confirm regression.

cheng: on it. will run baseline and new side-by-side with identical load generator. plan: 1) reproduce with 30s GPU-sampled capture 2) export timeline `nsys stats --report` and compare kernel lists 3) correlate NVTX kv metrics with kernel selection times.

maria: don't forget to collect cgroups/cpu usage and the runtime logs — sometimes the selector logs a reason at DEBUG level. set REDWOOD_LOG=debug on the runtime container.

kyle: once you have repro, add a tiny harness test in perf-suite that forces small warmup (simulate partial kv cache) and asserts stable kernel choice for 100 consecutive batches. that will catch regressions in CI.

cheng: action items: 
- rerun nsys with `--sample=gpu` `--sampling-frequency=2000` `--duration=30` and bracket NVTX warmup/steady ranges :eyes:
- run against `perf-baseline-20260310` and current image `ded-dev-latest` :rocket:
- gather runtime debug logs and attach timeline screenshots to the issue
- add perf-suite harness if repro is deterministic

dev-bot: noted. created issue PERF-897 and attached a checklist template.

maria: thanks — ping here when you have the two timelines. if we confirm regression we can roll back PR #4521 or add a targeted fix to the kernel selector.

cheng: will update with timelines + raw nsys `.qdrep`/`.nsys-rep` artifacts. thanks all.
